headline: High-risk pair: RD-Agent’s broad API/browser access and secret handling can amplify MemMachine context into leakage, conflicts, and unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, while RD-Agent can run browsers and uses broad network egress. That creates a plausible bridge where content from MemMachine can be fed into RD-Agent workflows, and browser-mediated content can be treated as instructions. No direct provenance controls are documented, so the interaction is risky but not proven high.
conditions: IF MemMachine content is forwarded through MCP into RD-Agent prompts or browser tasks
IF RD-Agent parses retrieved web or file content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP bridging between the agents for untrusted content
Add a fixed instruction/data delimiter in the handoff format
Require manual review of any browser-sourced text before reuse
Log and reject prompts containing role or tool directives from external content

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and RD-Agent handles financial reports, research papers, datasets, logs, and secrets while also using broad network egress. Because RD-Agent can send data to external APIs and MemMachine can expose context through MCP, the pair can leak sensitive material in default workflows unless tightly isolated.
conditions: IF MemMachine context is passed into RD-Agent prompts, logs, or browser tasks
IF RD-Agent forwards those inputs to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, or Kaggle APIs
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces and credentials
Redact long-term user facts before any handoff
Block secret-bearing files from RD-Agent inputs
Turn off external API calls for shared sensitive tasks
requires-engineering: add DLP/provenance filters on the handoff path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine can call APIs through REST/Python/MCP, and RD-Agent supports multiple instances plus broad API access and file logging. Their write surfaces overlap on external services and shared outputs, so concurrent updates can conflict even without a shared local filesystem. The profiles do not show locking, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external API, dataset, or log destination
IF multiple RD-Agent instances operate on the same project state without locks
mitigations: Assign separate output directories and API credentials
Serialize writes to shared resources
Use per-agent run IDs in filenames and records
Pause one agent during mutable operations
requires-engineering: add optimistic-locking or lease coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can supply long-lived context through MCP, and RD-Agent is a research automation system that can act on prompts, APIs, and browser results. If RD-Agent treats MemMachine output as authoritative, errors can cascade into research artifacts or external API actions. There is no documented verification step between them, so the interaction is materially risky.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes MemMachine output without an independent verification step
IF RD-Agent uses that output to generate reports, code, or API-driven actions
mitigations: Require a human review gate before RD-Agent acts on MemMachine output
Cross-check key facts against a second source
Mark MemMachine output as untrusted in the prompt template
Separate retrieval from action-taking steps
requires-engineering: add citation and validation enforcement

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, research papers, datasets, logs, and secrets. The profiles show different data classes and no shared residency or retention controls, so compliance mismatches are plausible if the same regulated data flows through both. Because the mismatch is not explicitly documented, medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is routed from MemMachine into RD-Agent logs or external APIs
IF retention or deletion obligations apply to the shared data class
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Minimize logging on both agents
Separate retention policies by workspace
Review vendor terms for each external API
requires-engineering: implement residency and deletion controls
